title: Quorum sensing involved in regulating biological phosphorus removal under two different addition modes of microplastics
description: Microplastics (MPs) in sewage sludge may promote pollutant dispersion in the environment, yet their impact on microbial metabolic interactions remains unclear. This study investigates the effects of polystyrene MPs (PS-MPs) o activated sludge and elucidates the regulatory role of quorum sensing (QS) under two dosing modes. Results showed that anaerobic phosphorus release decreased from 16.91 mg/L and 10.92 mg/L to 7.72 mg/L and 5.54 mg/L under 10 mg/L and 100 mg/L PS-MPs, respectively, while phosphorus removal efficiency dropped from 87.52% and 88.17% to 53.83% and 58.14%. Continuous dosing of 10 mg/L PS-MPs caused more persistent inhibition, whereas acetate uptake recovered faster under 100 mg/L PS-MPs. 10 mg/L PS-MPs impaired phosphorus metabolism more significantly than single high-dose exposure. Extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) increased steadily from 85.18 to 145.59 mg/g SS under the 10 mg/L group, but decreased initially then rose in the 100 mg/L group. The analysis of microbial community composition indicates that exposure to PS decreases the abundance of the dominant community PAOs and increases the species diversity. The correlation analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between the QS molecules C8-HSL and 3OC8-HSL and EPS components, particularly polysaccharides (PS) and proteins (PN) (P < 0.05), indicating that QS regulates EPS secretion and influences carbon and phosphorus metabolism through regulating the expression of key genes phbB, ppk and ppx. these findings offer insights for sustaining biological phosphorus removal and enhancing resilience against MPs-induced shocks.
